newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Kimber Q1 earnings seen weak.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Kimber Q1 earnings seen weak.

text.p: Mexican paper products manufacturer Kimberly Clark de Mexico (Kimber) is expected to post first quarter earnings adversely affected by a slow recovery in domestic consumption, a price war and seasonal factors, analysts said.
Kimberly-Clark de Mexico is partially owned by Kimberly-Clark Corp and is traded separately in Mexico.

A survey of three analysts gave an average first quarter sales forecast of 2.232 billion pesos and operating earnings of 623.19 millones de pesos, with residual net earnings totalling 535.27 million pesos, equivalent to 0.40 per share.

Analysts saw revenues undermined by Easter holidays coming early in 1997, and contracts to supply materials to schools due for delivery in the second quarter, rather than the first quarter as happened in 1996.

"The first quarter will be weak, but you need to take a longer term view with Kimber. It is one of the best companies in Mexico with a dominant market position," said Michel Morin, an analyst with Merrill Lynch in Mexico City.

"The report will be lacklustre, with a slight downward trend. This is justified as consumption of Kimber brands has fallen because purchasing power has yet to hit people's pockets," said an analyst from the Arka brokerage in Mexico City, who asked not to be named.
"Kimber has already indicated the early months of the year were difficult for the company as the quarter was cut short by Easter week," he added.

Comparisons with the first quarter of 1996 "would not be very valid" analysts said, as the company had since incorporated its merger with Compania Industrial San Cristobal (Crisoba) and was currently in the throes of asset sales.
Morin said a price war between paper companies would also eat into Kimber's earnings.

"The industry is running at excess capacity and that makes for tough competition and competitors lowered prices in 1996. Now Kimber wishes to lead the way, so they have not raised prices even though competitors have given signs they would like to," he said.

"Operating results will be hit by pulp prices which are still low and that will have to be passed on to prices for some articles," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst with the Bursametrica consultancy in Mexico City.
Analysts generally expected Kimber to be stronger during the remainder of the year, with cash flow bolstered by improved consumption and asset sales.
"We do, however, expect better earnings in coming quarters," Galvan added.
